html:
The Malagasy Uprising was a revolt against French rule that began on the night of 29 March 1947 in eastern Madagascar and was crushed by early 1949.

Bitterness over forced labour, the war effort and land taken for settlers ran deep. Rebels armed mostly with spears attacked French posts and plantations and held much of the east for months. French forces, including colonial troops from Africa, answered with massacres, torture and the burning of villages, and many died of hunger and disease in the forest.

Estimates of the dead range from about 11,000 to over 90,000. The leaders of the nationalist party were tried, though they had not ordered the rising. 29 March is a national day of remembrance in Madagascar, which gained independence under Philibert Tsiranana in 1960.
sum: The Malagasy Uprising was a revolt against French rule that began on the night of 29 March 1947 in eastern Madagascar and was crushed by early 1949.
